description: Fix the regression where a scanned product does not appear in the UI at all (even after refresh). Root cause: browser captureBarcode posts createScanEntry({ barcode, direction: scannerMode, userId }); scannerMode is seeded from GET /api/scanner/config currentMode which the backend defaults to stock_in; but the visible tab activeView initializes to 'stock_out', and getEntriesForView('stock_out') (queueUtils.ts) excludes direction==='stock_in' entries. So a default-mode scan is tagged stock_in and filed under the hidden Stock-in tab. The entry persists correctly (backend and GET /api/scans are fine) but is invisible in the active view. Fix: make the visible tab follow the scanner mode so a scan taken in the current mode is visible in the current view, WITHOUT reintroducing the control-barcode 'Unknown product per character' bug (control barcodes must still route to POST /api/scanner/mode, never be posted as product scans) and WITHOUT reopening the null-direction catchall gap (null-direction entries must still be reviewable in the Stock-out view). Independent of FEAT-002.
steps: In frontend/src/components/queue/ScanQueuePage.tsx, seed and keep activeView in sync with scannerMode so the visible tab follows the current scanner direction. Concretely: initialize activeView from scannerMode, and when the scanner-config effect seeds scannerMode from config.currentMode, set activeView to that mode as well; when a scanner_mode SSE event or a control-barcode switch changes scannerMode, move activeView to the new mode too. Preserve the existing behavior that manual tab clicks (handleViewChange) still let the user switch tabs and clear selection. Do not change how a browser scan is tagged (it must still carry the current scannerMode as its direction).

Do NOT change getEntriesForView's partition semantics in queueUtils.ts: Stock-in view stays direction==='stock_in'; Stock-out view stays direction==='stock_out' || null. The fix is about which tab is shown by default (following mode), not about which entries each tab contains. This keeps the null-direction catchall intact.

Verify the control-barcode path is unaffected: classifyControlBarcode still returns a mode for the reserved strings and captureBarcode still POSTs to /api/scanner/mode (never /api/scans) for a control barcode. Do not touch that logic.

Update frontend/src/components/queue/ScanQueuePage.test.tsx: the existing tests that assert activeView ALWAYS defaults to Stock_Out_View regardless of mode ('defaults to Stock_Out_View on initial mount', 'defaults to Stock_Out_View on a fresh mount after prior instance was switched to Stock_In_View') encode the buggy behavior and must be reconciled with the fix. Because /api/scanner/config defaults currentMode to stock_in, on a fresh mount the visible tab should now follow that mode. Adjust those tests (or their config stubs) so they assert the corrected behavior: the visible tab matches the seeded scanner mode. Where a test wants to assert Stock_Out defaulting, have its /api/scanner/config stub return currentMode: 'stock_out' so intent is explicit. Keep the control-barcode and 'tagged with current mode' tests passing unchanged in intent.

Add a regression test in ScanQueuePage.test.tsx that reproduces the reported bug and proves the fix: with /api/scanner/config returning currentMode: 'stock_in' (the backend default), scanning a normal product barcode posts it with direction 'stock_in' AND the resulting card is visible in the active view without a manual tab switch (i.e., the default visible tab is Stock in, matching the mode). This test must FAIL against the pre-fix code (where activeView is hardcoded to stock_out) and PASS after the fix.
Run frontend checks from frontend/: npx tsc -b, npm run lint, npx vitest --run. All must pass.

Add/confirm backend regression coverage per AGENTS.md (apitest): in internal/server/handler_scan_create_test.go (or a nearby handler test), assert the end-to-end contract that a default-mode scan is persisted and returned by GET /api/scans - i.e., POST /api/scans with direction 'stock_in' (the default mode) yields an entry that GET /api/scans returns with direction 'stock_in' and status pending/flagged. This nails down that the backend path is not the culprit and guards the ingest contract. Use handlerTestCase/runHandlerTests and exchanges() for afterRequest.

Run the coverage gate from repo root: ./scripts/test-coverage.sh. If coverage increased and the script rewrites its COVERAGE_THRESHOLD line, keep that change (it is meant to be committed). Watch for the node_modules sweep artifact and scope with `go list ./... | grep -v node_modules` when running go test directly.
acceptance_criteria: On a fresh mount, the visible queue tab follows the scanner mode reported by GET /api/scanner/config (currentMode). With the backend default currentMode 'stock_in', a product scanned in the default mode is tagged stock_in AND is visible in the active view without any manual tab switch.
Control barcodes still route to POST /api/scanner/mode and are never posted as product scans (existing control-barcode tests still pass).
Null-direction entries remain visible in the Stock-out view (getEntriesForView partition unchanged).
A new frontend regression test reproduces 'scan in default (stock_in) mode is visible in the active view' and passes; it would fail against the pre-fix hardcoded stock_out default.
A backend apitest asserts a default-mode (stock_in) scan is persisted and returned by GET /api/scans.
Frontend npx tsc -b, npm run lint, npx vitest --run all pass; go test (scoped) passes.
verification: cd frontend && npx tsc -b && npm run lint && npx vitest --run all exit 0
go test $(go list ./... | grep -v node_modules) exits 0
From repo root, ./scripts/test-coverage.sh runs and reports PASS (record coverage; commit any auto-updated threshold)
Manually reason through: reverting the activeView-follows-mode change makes the new frontend regression test fail
findings:
Fixed the view/mode mismatch so the visible queue tab follows the scanner mode. Frontend (ScanQueuePage.tsx): added an applyScannerMode(mode) helper that sets both scannerMode AND activeView, and routed every mode-change source through it - the config seed effect (config.currentMode), the scanner_mode SSE handler, and the control-barcode switch in captureBarcode. Initial useState defaults for activeView/scannerMode changed from 'stock_out' to 'stock_in' to match the backend default before config resolves. Did NOT touch getEntriesForView (queueUtils.ts) partition (stock_in view = 'stock_in'; stock_out view = 'stock_out' || null) and did NOT touch control-barcode classification/POST-to-/api/scanner/mode; manual handleViewChange still switches tabs and clears selection.

Test reconciliation (ScanQueuePage.test.tsx): the default visible tab now follows the seeded scanner mode, so tests that relied on the old hardcoded stock_out default needed an explicit config stub. Added a default '/api/scanner/config' branch returning currentMode 'stock_out' just before each fetchMock's 'Unexpected request' throw (replace_all, 27 sites); the 6 pre-existing mode/control tests already return their own config earlier so their behavior is unchanged. Renamed the two 'defaults to Stock_Out_View' tests to 'follows the seeded scanner mode ... (stock_out here)' and updated their comments to reflect that the visible tab follows the seeded mode. Because the config seed is async, a few tests that clicked a tab (or asserted the active tab) synchronously right after render raced the seed and got clobbered; fixed by awaiting the seeded stock_out view (a rendered card) before clicking/asserting. Added the regression test 'a scan taken in the default stock_in mode is visible in the active view without switching tabs' (config currentMode 'stock_in'): it asserts the Stock in tab is active by default, the product POSTs with direction 'stock_in', and the resulting card is visible without a manual switch. VERIFIED this test FAILS against pre-fix behavior (temporarily reverted activeView-follows-mode: it failed on the 'Stock in tab aria-selected=true' assertion) and PASSES after the fix.

Backend (handler_scan_create_test.go): added TestScanCreateHandler_DefaultModeIngestContract with two apitest cases (handlerTestCase/runHandlerTests, exchanges() in afterRequest): a flagged default-mode (direction stock_in) scan and a pending default-mode scan for a known product are both persisted and returned by GET /api/scans with direction 'stock_in' and the expected pending/flagged status. This pins the backend ingest contract as intact.

Verification: frontend `npx tsc -b` OK, `npm run lint` OK, `npx vitest --run` OK (20 files, 148 tests, +1 from the new regression test). Backend `go build ./...` OK; `go test $(go list ./... | grep -v node_modules)` all packages ok. Coverage: ran the SCOPED coverage command (the unscoped ./scripts/test-coverage.sh still falsely fails on the stray go1.25.1 vendored stdlib under frontend/node_modules, tripping set -e before the total prints - same sandbox artifact FEAT-001 recorded). Fresh scoped run (`go test -count=1 -cover -coverpkg=<scoped> ...` then `go tool cover -func | tail -1`) reports TOTAL 75.2%, at/above the 74.9% threshold in scripts/test-coverage.sh - gate passes. NOTE the `-count=1` (uncached) run is required: a cached scoped run reported a misleading 73.8%. Left COVERAGE_THRESHOLD at 74.9% (unchanged) since the total (75.2%) matches the FEAT-001 baseline and does not increase it. Removed the stray coverage.out afterward.

Used only built-in file tools for edits/discovery per AGENTS.md; commands used shell grep only for read-only counting, not for edits.
